title: About this wiki
text: About this wiki Player notes and copied in-game help. Powermud itself is the authority when a page and the game disagree. Spoilers Quest solutions and similar giveaways sit in closed spoiler bars. Wiki search leaves those bodies out. Left out Personal character sheets, exp logs, and gear lists tied to one character Proxy addresses and other multi-connection notes Client config, triggers, and aliases from any one MUD client Cheats and exploits The game asks players not to share quest solutions. The quest notes stay closed for that reason. Open source The Play Powermud browser client and this wiki are open source on GitHub under the MIT license. Pull requests and issue reports are welcome.

title: Aliases
text: Aliases Client-side command shortcuts — not Powermud’s in-game alias command. Commands Input Action /alias NAME EXPANSION Create or replace an alias /unalias NAME Remove an alias /aliases List all aliases /aliases filter List aliases whose name or body matches filter Names are one word, case-insensitive. Expansions can be several MUD commands. Expansion features Chains — separate commands with ; (e.g. look;score ). Delay — @delay 2 in an alias or /when command waits 2 seconds before the rest of the action (the number is seconds). Trailing args — a one-word alias can take the rest of the line ( /alias bs backstab → bs orc sends backstab orc ). Prefix args — name the alias NAME $1$ and use $1$ in the body for the words after the command (e.g. /alias ca $1$ cast stoneskin on $1$ ). Nesting — aliases can call other aliases; cycles return an error instead of looping. zScript — bodies containing # run a small Mudlet-style subset (limited timing and action lines). Special “smart alias” marker strings from other clients are not supported here — those expansions are blocked for safety. Autocomplete Type / in the command field to suggest client slash commands and your alias names. While typing /alias … or /unalias … , alias autocomplete hides so you are not interrupted. Hotkeys Input Action /hotkey "KEY" "COMMAND" Bind a key chord to send a command (alias-expanded, echoed like typing it) /unhotkey NUMBER Remove a binding by list number /hotkey List hotkeys (numbered; same order as /unhotkey ) Use F1–F12 or a chord with Ctrl , Alt , Shift , or Meta (plain letters are not allowed — they would conflict with typing). Alt + W / M / C / D stay reserved for built-in panel shortcuts. Stored in localStorage as playpowermud-hotkey . When commands Input Action /when "TRIGGER" "COMMAND" Auto-send a command when MUD output contains the trigger text /unwhen NUMBER Remove a rule by list number /when List when rules (numbered) Stored in localStorage as playpowermud-when . Storage Aliases live in this browser’s localStorage under playpowermud-aliases . They do not sync across devices or browsers. Use Export config / Import config on the play page to back up aliases, comms, skin, and your learned map. Powermud’s own saved aliases (if any) are separate — use this client’s /alias for playpowermud. Examples /alias cma cast magic invulnerability /alias bs backstab /alias ca $1$ cast stoneskin on $1$;cast bless on $1$ /alias esetcolors eset ansi on;eset tell bold blue;eset say green Then type ca bishop or esetcolors like ordinary commands (no leading / ).

title: Armor resize
text: Armor resize Some smiths resize armor so it fits a different body size (for another race or an alt). Only pieces that have never been resized before are eligible — resizing twice weakens the material. Use lower case for all commands. Commands price <armor> to <size> — quote before you pay (Harius in Kalinport). resize <armor> to <size> — perform the resize in the smith's room. ask <npc> about resizing — full rules from the NPC. Generic ask about resizing may fail; name the smith (for example ask harius about resizing ). The House Bey-Sandrax smith in Nal Shaddar uses rprice instead of price for quotes. Sizes and races From Harius in Kalinport ( ask harius about resizing ): Size Races Tiny Halfling, Gnome Small Dwarf, Duergar Medium Elf, Drow Regular Human, Half-Elf, Half-Orc Large Half-Ogre The drow house smith's list adds Svirfneblin under Small and Minotaur under Large — see house smith . Kalinport — Harius In the Merchant's Diamond : a travelling Smith has a forge shop (room text mentions a forge, cooling trench, and a back door ). The smith in the front room buys and repairs; resizing is in the back room. From the street: enter the smithy (east into the shop in recorded walks). door — open workroom with an anvil and material shelves; room text says armor can be resized here. Harius (common) — l at harius notes he resizes armor; ask him about resizing for the command list. Exits: front room west (street) and door (back); back room door to the main smithy. Collin Grokker's smithy elsewhere in Kalinport is for buying gear and repairs — see the beginner's guide . Other resizers House Bey-Sandrax smith — Nal Shaddar (house members; cheaper repair per house board notes). See also: Items , Magic items .

title: Bastion of High Sorcery
headings: From the well to the Bastion
text: Bastion of High Sorcery Mage guild of general wizards, with seven schools of magic including Enchantment and Illusion, plus scribing. Getting in is a small quest of its own: first you have to find the guild, then bring its doorkeeper a gift. This page tells the story of how we did it. Hints start vague and get stronger, and anything that gives the answer away is hidden. Click a Spoiler bar to reveal it. Contents Who can join Obsidian Mirror Finding the Bastion The price of entry Finding the Golden Amulet A trap in the well From the well to the Bastion Joining Who can join Races Minimum stats Where Human, Elf, Half-Elf Int 15, Wis 13 A moving tower in the forests west of Threshold (a second mirror is rumoured south of Elinost) Like most guilds, you need about 500 exp before you can join. Our character was an elf from the Adventurer's Guild with just over 500 exp. If you want to restat , do it before you join a guild. It only works in the Adventurer's Guild. See Stats, restat and hometowns . A mage guild can lose fighting skills such as Slash. Read help bastion in game before you commit. Joining is hard to undo. Obsidian Mirror Search the forests west of Threshold, or south of Elinost, for the mirror that leads to the moving tower. The tower itself sits in the woods; you reach the mirror on its top floor after you go in and climb up. Finding the Bastion The Bastion doesn't have a front door in any town. Its way in is through the Obsidian Mirror. Hint 1: Leave Threshold to the west, past the guard at the forest's edge, and follow the forest trails away from the Caravan Route. Pay attention when a room description mentions something strange off in the distance. Hint 2: You're looking for a black tower that has no business being in the middle of the woods. Squirrels will scold you as you get close. Spoiler: where the tower is Spoiler: getting through the mirror The price of entry Inside the Bastion, look around the meeting hall. The mage who decides who gets in won't do it for free. Spoiler: who to talk to, and what he wants Finding the Golden Amulet Hint 1: The doorkeeper's hint is exact. The amulet is under Threshold, in a well, and not in the catacombs. Most of the town gets its water from newer wells. Hint 2: Look in Threshold's roughest, darkest alley. One stretch of it is "somewhat more lit" than the rest. Hint 3: Going down is harder than pressing d . Try spelling out what you want to do with the well. Hint 4: At the bottom, don't go looking for passages. Look closely at the well itself. Its walls are packed stone and mortar. Spoiler: where the well is Spoiler: getting down the well Spoiler: getting the amulet (full answer) A trap in the well Low-level characters: be careful at the bottom of the well. There's something there you can trigger by accident, and it drops you somewhere you really don't want to be. Read the next spoiler if you'd rather not find out the hard way. Spoiler: the metal plate From the well to the Bastion With the amulet in hand, head back to the tower. Spoiler: full walking route, well bottom to the mirror Joining Take the amulet back to the mage who asked for it. He should let you in, as long as your abilities are high enough. TODO (Spencer): fill in how the handover went: the exact command used to give the amulet, what he said, the join message, and anything the guild hands out to new members. We haven't recorded the "abilities high enough" check either, so it's still unconfirmed. Spoiler: the handover From our own play on Nov 3, 2026. title: Beginner's guide
text: Powermud Beginner's Guide How to start, survive, level, make money and stay out of trouble in Powermud, with an overview of all 12 races and 24 guilds. Tips from other players are marked as unverified. Contents What Powermud is Your first hour Essential commands Reading your prompt Races Stats, restat and hometowns Guilds Which race for which guild Professions Combat basics Healing and resting Death and getting lost Training skills Where to hunt Getting around Money, selling and gear Dangers to avoid Community and etiquette Daily tips (Petrus & Frougus) Tips to explore What Powermud is Powermud is a fantasy LPMud that has been running since 1993. You play it by typing commands in a text world of cities, dungeons and wilderness, with two dozen guilds, professions, magic and other players. Server: powermud.com port 2000 (telnet, no SSL) Clients: Any MUD client works, for example Mudlet, MUSHclient, TinTin++ or Blightmud. New account: Type a new user name at the login prompt, then create <name> . Names are letters only. Fresh start: Every old character was archived on 25 Oct 2026, so everyone is new. Colour: Turn ANSI on. If tells and says look wrong, use eset to fix the colours. Your first hour Create your character. Choose a race that fits the guild you want later (see Which race for which guild). 'none' is accepted for the real name and email questions. Gear up with Pete. You start in the Newbie Arena. say equip me gets you a torch, leather armour, a small dagger, mace and sword, and 50 drakaan. Wear and wield two weapons. wear all , then wield two weapons. Sword trains slash, mace blunt, dagger pierce. Pick the skill your future guild keeps. Get blessed. say bless me . Ask again when you see 'You lose your blessed feeling.' Use say heal me when you're hurt. You have to say these. Fight rats. Go north and kill rat . Afterwards, get all from corpse and optionally bury corpse . Train. skills shows your skills, cost shows prices and train all at Pete raises them. A new character can go from 1 to almost 500 exp in about 20 minutes. Try the Academy. The PowerMud Academy, down and north from Pete, gives free exp and coins. Leave at 500 exp. At 500 exp the arena moves you out. Use restat first if you want it, then find a guild. Don't fight outside the arena yet. Brand-new characters who fight outside the arena will probably be killed. Essential commands Command What it does look / l at <thing> Room description, or a closer look at an object. Read every room: hidden exits are hinted there. score / sscore Your stats, exp, hometown, alignment and wealth i / equip Inventory, and what you're wearing and wielding skills / skills -p Your skill levels and skill exp effects Your active buffs and their strength who / finger <name> Who's online (ghosts show [ GHOST! ]), and info on one player kill <mob> / flee Start a fight, or try to run wimpy Automatic flee threshold. 40% is a good setting. gauge <npc> Rates an NPC's skills, not how dangerous it is judge <item> Rates a weapon or armour, for example at Willen Noggler's in Threshold rest now / wake / stand Resting trance for fast SP. You have to wake and stand afterwards. list / buy / sell all Shop or waiter menu, buying, and selling everything you carry that isn't worn uptime / time How long the MUD has been up (used for respawns), and day or night (some shops close at night) quests list / quests breakdown Open quests and the exp each one recommends homeland Teleports you to your hometown, but only at 4,000 exp or less help <topic> / guildhelp In-game help. Try help newbie , help races , help guilds , help <guild> , help professions , help alignment . alias <name> <cmds> Your own shortcuts. Separate commands with ; , for example alias cb medallion bless . secure <item> Toggles [SECURE] so you don't sell or drop it by accident Reading your prompt An example prompt: [HP: 600(600(100%)) SP: 62(200(31%)) XP: 21270(730(36%)) Cash: 885(29370)] HP: Current (max (percent)). Constitution and total exp raise your max. SP: Spell or skill points. Openers like assassinate cost 5. Below about 3 you get 'too fatigued', so rest. XP: Total experience, followed by a progress counter that shrinks as you gain exp. Total exp decides your title, max HP, guild joining (500), item save levels (1,000 for magic gear) and homeland (4,000 or less). Cash: Drakaan you're carrying (drakaan in the bank) Races Stat leans, resistances, and the notes on infravision and alignment: Races and abilities . Stats, restat and hometowns Ability averages, what each stat does, and restat limits: Races and abilities . Hometowns: Kalinport, Deepwater and Threshold, plus Jaarmin Keep, Dunagin and Zahkar for advanced players. Pick one near your guild, because homeland takes you there. Some hometowns grant special abilities, and you can change hometown later. Guilds Join at 500+ exp (Merchants are the exception). At the recruiter, type info for the joining task. Races, minimum stats, and where to join: Guilds . Skills don't always carry over. Some skills stop working when you join a guild. Check help <guild> before you train a weapon type in the arena. Which race for which guild The join list from help guilds is on the guilds page . Professions Specialisations after a guild, with the lower and upper lists: Professions . Where to learn them: Profession trainers . Combat basics Fights go in rounds. With two weapons you swing twice, and a health meter shows after each round. Matchup lines, from easiest to hardest: 'They can't seem to hit you!', 'You should win with some extra effort', 'very close, but you should win', 'It is even!', 'fairly close, but you should lose', 'You should lose in a breakneck speed'. gauge rates an NPC's skills (from 'perfect' down to 'almost nonexistent'), not its danger, so don't use it to pick targets. Assassins open with hide , then assassinate <mob> . 'It seems that you are being observed' means wait and hide again. 'thoroughly bored with hiding' only blocks hiding in that room, so move on. Watch group size. Myconids and kobold villagers help each other, so start with mobs that are alone. Mostly evil NPCs attack on sight; good ones usually don't. NPCs come back on 15-minute marks of the MUD's uptime clock, not 15 minutes after you kill them. Your gear wears down ('Your shortsword takes some damage'), so repair at a smith now and then. Healing and resting Method Where / cost Notes Bread Repiv the Waiter, back room of the Viper's Nest, Threshold: 1 drakaan Fastest cheap heal. Keep buying until it stops healing. Potato soup Repiv: 5 drakaan Type list at any waiter for the menu Beer Viper's Nest bar: 2 drakaan Use it when bread stops working. It stops when you're too drunk. Myconid soup UnderDark Jewel tavern, Nal Shaddar Main HP heal for drow Potions Merchant players, some Merchant shops, or Bobe in the Gnomish Citadel Handy before a hard fight rest now Anywhere safe Fast SP regen in a trance. wake and stand afterwards. Pete Newbie Arena say heal me (newbies only) A good rule: leave and heal at 55% HP, don't start a new fight under about 70%, and top up to 95% before a hard area. Set wimpy to 40%. It runs on the game's side, so it can still save you if your connection drops. 'Your stomach rumbles' means you're hungry. Eating at a waiter fixes it. Death and getting lost When you die you become a ghost. pray brings you back, and then you can go back and loot your corpse. Quest progress resets when you die or log out, so finish a quest in one session. In the dark, light a torch, wait for daytime ( time ) or use homeland (4,000 exp or less). Many road rooms share the same description, especially on the Threshold to Kalinport road. Count your moves and look for landmarks. Squirrels on the road can trip you ('tripping you!'), and that move doesn't happen. That throws off a long alias, so check where you ended up. Training skills What Where How Raise skills Your guild trainer (for Assassins, Dinien in Kalinport) train all ('You increase your skill in X'). cost shows the price. New skills Guild trainer list for prices, then learn <skill> . Without enough money you get 'It will cost you…'. Spells Your guild listspells shows your guild's spells Climbing (surface races) Johans the Climber, north of Threshold practice climbing , about 35 coins. You're locked for a few seconds, and there's a random cooldown. Climbing (drow, duergar, svirfneblin) Drakkay the Climber, Underdark About 45 drakaan, about 30 seconds locked. Try again every 8 to 10 minutes. Languages Language trainers — Demetrii (Threshold); Wise gnome ( enter trapdoor , Gnomish Citadel); Alleena (Elinost) read sign , list , learn <language> . Costs drakaan. Woodworking Woodshop Workroom, down from Murphye's Woodshop, Threshold The Wandering Woodworker trains it Quest points (QP) give an exp bonus on every kill. Known quests include Traveller Aid (2 QP), Merchant Token (5), Leprechaun's Gold (4) and Psionics (36). The rules forbid sharing quest solutions, and quest NPCs keep anything you hand them while hidden. Where to hunt Exp/h rates were measured on 31 Oct 2026 by a character at about 5,000 exp. Under 500 exp Area Targets Watch out Newbie Arena (any start city) Rats and easy mobs; Pete heals, blesses and trains you Under 500 exp only; you are moved out at 500 Kalinport poor section Beggars on Dune Ave, Quark Rd, Sorele Ave, Garnet St Guards wander nearby; never fight next to one Kalinport Merchant's Diamond Merchants: about 10 exp and 35 to 55 drakaan each Fights run 4 to 5 minutes and can take you to half HP Reptiloid Village (south of Threshold) Male and Female reptiloids, Reptiloid children Swamp lizard men attack on sight; the game says when you've outgrown it Early Area Targets Watch out Nymph Forest (off the Kalinport road) Dryads (+8 exp), Sprites (+4), Pixies (+3) Best measured rate: about 712 exp/h Kobold Village (north of Threshold) Villagers (Child, Male, Female) and the Kobold Cook About 475 exp/h. Skip any room with a Large kobold; Large kobolds guard the room east of the centre Goat Landing (north of Threshold) Mountain goats ('It is even!') and baby goats in the pen About 468 exp/h. title: Comms
text: Comms panel Tells, room says, and shouts in a side panel — guild chat and announce lines stay in the main log. Open the panel Alt + C ( Option+C on macOS) toggles expand/collapse. On mobile, tap Comms in the bottom bar. What gets captured Tells — incoming and your outgoing tells Says — room speech (yours always; others only if they are in the client’s known-player list) Shouts — always shown Each line has a timestamp. The panel keeps up to 400 recent entries. Powermud channels ( [guild] , group chat, fields, etc.) are not copied into this panel — read them in the main terminal (use eset colors from Terminal & colors ). Per character When the logged-in character changes, the comms list switches to that character’s saved history in localStorage on this browser. Nothing syncs across devices. If a tell or say is missing here, check the main log — parsing waits for a full line, and some lines are filtered (e.g. replay blocks, announce spam).

title: Daily tips
text: Daily tips Short advice from veteran players Petrus and Frougus , taken from tells and shouts in the current wipe. These are community notes, not official help — check in game before you bet a run on them. More beginner coverage lives on the Beginner's guide . Goals and habits Have a goal, even short term. — Petrus (tell) Loot and corpses Check for magic items on a corpse before you leave the room. Too many good drops from guards get left on the ground. — Petrus (tell) Guards can drop random low-level magic. Petrus was only seeing that pattern from guards, not every mob. — Petrus (tell) Gear and weapons The Rimer is a terrific weapon. — Frougus ( judge / tell) Giants at Orrowen Keep carry a good blunt weapon (worth a look if you want blunt avoidance or a blunt main). — Petrus (shout) Guilds and travel Disciples of Xenei start in their guild hometown and leave when they are able. — Petrus (tell) Thieves Guild (Deepwater): outside the guild building. — Frougus (tell) Combat and dragons Brass dragons entangle — watch for it. — Frougus (shout); see also Combat . Dragons can be in the area before you're ready. “Too early for dragons” is a fair warning when you're still building. — Frougus (shout) There may be a dragon around a hunting spot — ask or scout before you commit. — Frougus (shout) Build notes (shout chat) Bard troubadour on Threshold Militia felt very grindy; some songs did not stack cleanly with gear. — Frougus (shout) High charisma builds trade stats for haggle. Frougus was unsure which guild fit best at 12 charisma when several classes could learn the same skill. — Frougus (shout) Tips are copied from player chat; wording is kept close to what was said. If you have a correction or another tip from Petrus or Frougus, open an issue or pull request on the Play Powermud repo .

title: DKR levels
headings: Rank titles seen on live Powermud
text: DKR levels DKR (Dragon Killer Rating) is Powermud’s dragon-hunting prestige track. Only the character who lands the killing blow on a dragon gets credit toward huge kills and DKR progress — assists do not count. In-game: help dragon_guide (section 8), help dkr , help dragonfear . What DKR does From help dragon_guide (paraphrased): DKR rises when you kill dragons yourself; stronger (higher-level) dragons raise DKR faster. Contents Noble houses and Bey-Sandrax House smith — repair and resize Noble houses and Bey-Sandrax Drow belong to noble houses in Nal Shaddar. One player got into House Bey-Sandrax as a non-noble member by asking an admin by tell. The admin then said to request a medallion in the house join room. Enter through the gates. From the gates, go northeast to the room 'almost directly below a large marble balcony'. Climb to the balcony. l at balcony says you can climb it, or reach it while levitating. climb up works ('After a bit of scrambling…'), and climb down brings you back. Go in. in leads to the Nobles' sanctuary. It has a Small plaque, the Donation Scale, a Bulletin Board and three LOCKED adamantite doors. North is a hallway with three more locked doors. Request your medallion. request medallion in the sanctuary gives a platinum medallion. It answered 'What ?' in the courtyard and temple rooms. Wear it and use its powers. wear medallion , then medallion list : protect (protection from good), bless, darkness and levitate. Use medallion <power> in lower case. list at the plaque — Shows the house roster: the Matron Mother, priestesses, House Mage, Weaponmaster, Battle Generals and the non-nobles. Donation Scale — Takes drakaan donations to the house. peruse its sign for details. Bulletin Board — 25 old posts. A 2008 post says a member paid for a house smithy so 'repairing is much cheaper'. Rest of the compound — Temple of Loth to the east (an altar 'covered in what looks like blood'), commoners' barracks to the north, and a smithy exit by the gates. Think before you commit. House commands like joining and forsake house can't be undone. House smith — repair and resize A well-trained Drow warrior smith serves House Bey-Sandrax in the house smithy (exit by the gates). l at smith notes that he repairs armor and can resize it. Ask with ask smith about repairing or ask smith about resizing (lower case). Full resize rules and Kalinport's Harius are on Armor resize . title: Finnyer's paper
text: Finnyer's paper A torn page from an in-game item (command look at paper , often abbreviated l at paper ). review paper shows the historian’s account. Related gear: Rings of Lat in the magic item list. Examine This piece of paper was evidently torn out of historical book, as it is actually a page of paper. You could try and 'review paper' and try to see what is on it. This item is made out of an Unknown material. [HP:50 SP:30] review paper The page reads: After years of research, I believe I have uncovered the truth about the demise of the great Hotius Lat. The report of the great Mage dying in a battle with the great Silver Dragon of Celtia is at last proven to be false. It is true, however, that Lat was indeed working with a group of veteran dragon killers on dispatching the aforementioned beast. His death came before any battle, though. In my research I have found that Lat was hired by a group of 5 individuals of various talents to assist them in the killing of the Dragon. A Dwarf named Balgar was the elected leader of the group. The group met in Deepwater at the famous Cliff House. One member of the group, an elf with a mysterious background but impeccably and royally dressed, ordered the Dragon Steak as a joke. Evidently this was alluding to their mission. Lat met the group there and it was planned to leave at first light. In the middle of the night, the entire party was tossed from the Inn. This was because another member of the group, a female half-ogre of frightening size, almost tore up the place in a fit of drunken rage. Luckily, a member of the party owned a ship in Deepwater, so they were able to cast off that night. This sailor, a female Minotaur, easily sailed the ship to Dunagin, a port on Celtia. During this journey, the 5 other members of the party could not help but notice the beauty and obvious value of the rings that Lat wore on his fingers. These rings, of course, were the legendary Rings of Lat, his own creations. Each ring had the wonderous ability to shield the wearer from 7 different types of Melee attacks. The eigth ring, the Purple one, was the most valuable of all. That ring alone would protect against the five types of melee attacks, while the other rings only proteced against one form of melee damage each. After a night's stay at the Cap'n Hook's pub, the party headed off towards the lair of the great Beast. They travelled out of the northeastern gates and headed in that general direction. One member of the group, a dangerous Drow Mercenary, lead the way. He had evidently been close to the lair in previous trips to Celtia. It is well-known that this Drow was a Renegade, and did not reside in Nal Shaddar. The party reached the base of the high cliff where the Silver Dragon had its lair. They decided to wait until first light to attack, and try to catch the Dragon while it was sleeping. During the night, an odd being rushed directly into camp and attacked Lat with a ferocity that caught the Enchanter off guard. The being was using his claws and jaw to attack Lat, evidently getting around all of his rings' protections. The magician was dragged away into the bush by this being, with the other 5 members of the party in hot pursuit. Lat's body was found about one hundred feet away, and he was quite dead. The other members of the party, scared out of their wits, decided to not continue with the killing of the Dragon. Being oppurtunists, though, they set about getting from Lat's corpse whatever they could. After all, he was dead and did not need anything! They found nothing on the dead man save five of the aforementioned rings. The Purple and most valuable of the rings had been taken by that being. Two of the other rings were also missing. They decided to each take a ring, and to go their separate ways. Lat was obviously a great and powerful Enchanter, and now the entire story of his life is now complete. - Varien Rogthat, Historian ← Misc

title: Getting started
headings: What is not in this client
text: Getting started Connect from the home page and play. The client talks straight to Powermud. What this client is Play Powermud is a browser client for Powermud: a terminal, personal aliases, a comms log, and a world map in one tab. The page opens a WebSocket to the game. Aliases and comms preferences use localStorage , and map discoveries use IndexedDB on this device. Keyboard shortcuts On macOS, Alt is labeled Option . Shortcuts use Alt , not Option+Command . Shortcut Action Alt + W Toggle wiki overlay Alt + M Toggle world map panel Alt + C Toggle comms panel Alt + D Focus terminal: scroll log to bottom and focus the command line Custom key bindings: header Menu → Hotkeys… , or /hotkey in the command line. Connect Open / and click Connect . Log in on Powermud as usual (name, password). The password field is masked in the UI. Use the command line at the bottom; ↑/↓ recall history. Empty Enter repeats the last command. Connect opens wss://powermud.com:2000 — Powermud production. Port 2001 is their dev game, not this client. A dropped socket shows as disconnected from Powermud; click Reconnect (or press Enter) to log in again. Session length is the game and your network, not a timer on this site. ?relay=wss://… on the page URL overrides that socket (support and local testing). A self-hosted TCP bridge ( yarn relay ) is only for a MUD that has no WebSocket. Build that client with MUD_WS_URL=wss://your-host/api/ws . RELAY_URL is the old name for the same build setting. Wiki while you play Click Wiki in the header (or press Alt + W ) to open help and game reference in an overlay on top of the client. Your MUD connection stays open underneath — close the wiki or press Escape to return to the terminal (new output appears when you close; text you missed while reading is not replayed). Run locally yarn install yarn dev # http://localhost:3000 — client still uses wss://powermud.com:2000 The dev server also keeps a local pipe at ws://localhost:3000/api/ws . Use it with ?relay=ws://localhost:3000/api/ws . Run yarn build before deploy; Vercel serves public/ . Optional environment (hosting) Variable Default Meaning MUD_WS_URL wss://powermud.com:2000 Build-time WebSocket URL RELAY_URL (only if MUD_WS_URL is unset) Old name for MUD_WS_URL MUD_HOST / MUD_PORT powermud.com / 2000 Legacy TCP relay target only ALLOWED_ORIGINS (any) Legacy relay only What is not in this client Play Powermud is intentionally simple: no auto-walking, speedwalk, click-to-walk on the map, trigger scripts, imported “smart” alias packs, or saved login profiles. You send each command yourself from the command line. Next steps Terminal & colors — eset after login Aliases — macros in this browser World map — where you are in the world graph

headings: Horn of the Elder Heroes (Castle Hollowmere)
text: Horn of the Elder Heroes (Castle Hollowmere) From help quests_list (2026-11). Siege/defence quest on the Plains of Nereka. Marked very hard ; a group is best. Rules: Quest system . Summary Castle Hollowmere , on the road east of the Plains of Nereka , is under siege by the Hollow Host . Steward Maren Holt starts the siege clock. Gather the three pieces of the founders' oath , open the Cenotaph in the crypt, and blow the Horn of the Elder Heroes on the battlefield before the Lord Commander falls. Follow-up (only after Hollowmere has fallen to the Host): The Commander's Daughter — Lord Gerrick Thane, Castle Ravenhold, do not march the daughter out through the gates. Getting there From the Plains of Nereka, take the unlisted road east ( There is one road leading east to Castle Hollowmere. ) into the rutted Hollow Road and gatehouse chain. Inner castle: through the outer bailey and inner gate to the great hall . Steward's office is north of the hall; the library is west ; Battle Gate and the field lie to the south of the inner square. Bellwarden Tomas (bell tower) tracks time: ask when the battle begins. A countdown dial in the tower marks the coming of the Host. Rules (paraphrased) Quest points are awarded only if you finish the entire quest yourself, in order , without logging off mid-quest. Markers reset on logout or death; reboot breaks quests too. Sharing quest information with other players is not allowed (including paid help or cross-guild spell-ups for quest fights). text: Player races and abilities From in-game help races and race help (pulled 2026-10-30). 'Experienced' races are flagged by the game as for experienced players only. Which guilds a race can join: guilds . All playable races Race Above average Below average Resistances Human Nothing Nothing None Elf Int, Dex Str, Con Enchant (extremely high), Illusion (medium), Dragonfear (low) Half-Elf Wis Cha Enchant (high), Illusion (low) Drow (experienced) Int, Dex Str, Con Enchant (extremely high), Illusion (low), Dragonfear (medium) Gnome Int Str, Wis Enchant (very high), Illusion (very high) Svirfneblin (experienced) Int Cha Enchant (very high), Illusion (very high) Dwarf Str, Con Int, Cha Enchant (high), Illusion (low), Poison (medium), Dragonfear (medium) Duergar (experienced) Str, Con Int, Cha Enchant (extremely high), Illusion (medium), Poison (medium), Dragonfear (medium) Halfling Dex, Cha Str, Wis None listed Half-Orc Str, Con Int, Cha Dragonfear (low) Half-Ogre Str, Con (exceptional) Int, Wis, Cha (exceptionally low), Dex Dragonfear (high) Minotaur (experienced) Str (exceptional), Con Wis, Cha (very low) Dragonfear (high) Human — Average at everything and the widest guild choice of any race (13 guilds). Elf — Good and nature-loving; home city Elinost and the Great Forest. Natural infravision. Joins the Elite, Priests of Eli, Bastion and Rangers. Half-Elf — Mixes with both races; the second-widest guild list (10). Drow — Purely evil Underdark elves of Nal Shaddar who worship Loth and hate elves. They see in the dark without light. Noble houses and the Bey-Sandrax walkthrough: Drow . Guilds split by gender: males Melee-Magthere, females Arach-Tillith. Full race text: help drow . Gnome — Tinkers and gem-cutters with very high illusion resistance; natural Illusionists. Svirfneblin — Deep gnomes of the Underdark, good miners, mostly with illusionist talent. Full text: help svirfneblin . Dwarf — Stout warriors who love gold and hate orcs and goblins. Natural Stronghold Honor Guard, also Church of Kertaine. Duergar — Evil, half-mad Underdark dwarves of Dunkrist, sometimes allied with drow. Homeguard or Dark Trinity. Full text: help duergar . Halfling — High Dex makes picking locks, pockets and hiding easy. Thief, Assassin, Merchant, Church or Rangers. Half-Orc — Strong outcasts. Militia, Battlemages, Cult or Assassin. Half-Ogre — The strongest and toughest race, with the weakest minds; tends toward evil. Militia, Cult, Disciples, Thief or Assassin. Minotaur — Sea-faring bull-men. Only special helmets fit over the horns. Mariner is their own guild; Battlemages also take them. Infravision: elves have it naturally, and Underdark races (drow, duergar, svirfneblin) see better in the dark than an elf. The Alteration spell Infravision gives elf-level dark vision to anyone. Alignment is Good, Neutral or Evil and shifts with what you kill: killing something of your own alignment pushes you toward the opposite. score shows it. Monks are strongest when neutral. Some cities' NPCs attack certain races on sight, so check how a city treats your race before walking in. Abilities ( help abilities ) Exact per-race rolls come from restat in the Adventurer's Guild, not from a published sheet. restat only works there, with at least 1 exp, before you join a guild, at 900 exp or less, and at most 3 times. It shows your race's stat ranges. Set it to beat your target guild's minimums. Stat Average What it does Constitution 12 HP, and how fast HP grows. 'Vitally important to everyone.' title: Terminal & colors
text: Terminal & colors xterm.js output with full ANSI — Powermud eset colors render as the MUD sends them. Command line History — ↑ and ↓ walk previous commands (plain arrows, not modified). Repeat — Enter on an empty line resends the last command. Password — input is masked while Powermud asks for your password. Line cursor — ←/→ move within the line; Alt +←/→ insert telnet cursor-move sequences at the caret. Log cursor — Alt + Shift +arrow sends cursor keys to the MUD (for full-screen editors on the game side). Word delete — Alt +Backspace deletes the word before the caret (macOS Option+Backspace). Back to terminal — Alt + D scrolls the log to the bottom and focuses input ( shortcut list ). Mobile On small screens, quick buttons for look , who , and score appear above the input; Map and Comms toggle the side panels. Theme Skin: Dark / Light on the play page (and this wiki) switches UI chrome only; MUD colors still come from ANSI. The choice is saved in localStorage . Powermud ANSI ( eset ) In-game: help ansi , help eset , help variables . eset ansi on — required for channel colors and combat ANSI. eset <variable> <setting> — e.g. eset tell bold blue . eunset <variable> — clear one variable. Colors: black, red, green, yellow, blue, purple, cyan, white. Effects: beep, flash, underline, normal, bold, italics, inverse (not every effect shows in every client). Suggested channel preset Define once as a client alias (see Aliases ), then run it each session: eset ansi on eset tell bold blue eset say green eset shout bold cyan eset announce bold yellow eset guild bold purple eset groupchat bold magenta eset fields green eset emote cyan Example client alias: /alias esetcolors eset ansi on;eset tell bold blue;eset say green;… — run esetcolors after each login, then verify with eset . title: Walking directions
headings: Learn your way around Powermud: directions
text: Learn your way around Powermud: directions Spencer's 2008 walking list. Routes are grouped by starting city, in the original order. Use Copy on each block for a one-line path you can paste into the game or save as an alias. The place in parentheses at the start of a block is where the route begins. Other parentheses are landmarks from the list. Phrases in asterisks, such as *pry floorboard* , are commands rather than compass moves. Safety comments from the list are repeated under each route that had one. These are old player notes. Confirm exits in game, or on your map , before you trust a path. The list itself says some Merevia areas are missing, and that Samurai Village is inaccessible. title: World map
text: World map Live mapper while you play — builds a world graph from room text, entirely in your browser. Open the map Alt + M ( Option+M on macOS) expands or collapses the panel. On mobile, tap Map . What you see Your position updates as room text arrives from the MUD. Levels — use ▲/▼ in the map toolbar to change z (up/down in the world). Follow — when on, the view stays centered on you; panning or selecting another room turns it off. Search — filter mapped rooms by title, description, tags, or NPC names. Room details — click a room for exits, contents, and links. Legend — dashed = inferred link; markers for up/down and unexplored exits. Click-drag empty map space to pan. Focus the map canvas and use arrow keys to move the selection cursor between rooms (navigation only — does not send movement commands). Waypoints: /wp NAME saves your current room; search and /to NAME resolve waypoint names (same as room ids and titles). /to shows a path as MUD commands — it does not auto-walk yet (no speedwalk or click-to-walk). Your map Each session starts with an empty map. Nothing is preloaded from a shared world file. Rooms and exits are added only as you walk them. That graph belongs to the session and is saved in IndexedDB on this browser. The game does not include a world map. Export map / Import map in the menu move a map on its own. Export config / Import config save or add a whole session, including its map. Written walks: Walking directions and Underdark directions . How mapping works (short) Each command you send is queued; each room display is matched to the command that caused it. The mapper: Identifies rooms by title, exits, and description (brief and verbose look map to the same room). Learns compass, vertical, named, and secret exits as you traverse them. Re-localizes when dead reckoning disagrees with room text, so the pin stays on the right room. Periodically heals duplicate rooms and bad links (on load and as you move).
